articles.title: 5 Marvel Teams That Deserve a Comeback More Than Ever
articles.summary: Marvel Comics was the bestselling purveyor of superheroes for ages, but that has changed in the mid '20s. DC is on top and the House of Ideas is floundering. However, one place where they've managed to keep fans reading is their team books. Marvel is putting out some fantastic team books right now, with Fantastic […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics was the bestselling purveyor of superheroes for ages, but that has changed in the mid '20s. DC is on top and the House of Ideas is floundering. However, one place where they've managed to keep fans reading is their team books. Marvel is putting out some fantastic team books right now, with Fantastic Four, X-Men, Uncanny X-Men , and Avengers all impressing various parts of the fandom. The House of Ideas has always had some excellent teams; as great as the Justice League or Justice Society or Legion of Superheroes are, Marvel's teams are often just a little better. The publisher has decades of excellent team comics under their belt.

One could make the argument that the A-list teams are doing well because they are the A-list teams, but it's much simpler than that – they put the best creators on those books. Marvel is full of great teams that they aren't really doing anything with despite having the creators to make them work. The publisher needs a shot in the arm and these teams could give it to them. These five Marvel teams deserve a comeback, giving the House of Ideas more weapons in the sales war.

Guardians of the Galaxy was MCU perfection and it made the team a household name. However, it wasn't using the original version of the Guardians of the Galaxy, it was using the rebooted one that had been introduced 8 years before in Annihilation . This became the version of the team that Marvel Comics started using and there's an entire generation of Marvel fans who have no idea that they aren't the originals. The first version of the team isn't from the present, but the 31st (well, originally 30th) century.

In this future, the Earth was invaded by the Badoon, resulting in humanity being enslaved by the alien conquerors. The Guardians of the Galaxy –Vance Asto, Martinex, Charlie-13, and Yondu – fought to save humanity, with members like Starhawk, Nikki, Aleta, and Stakar joining up. They'd sometimes come back to the present, hanging out with the Avengers and other groups of heroes. The team has been all but forgotten, but honestly, give Al Ewing a chance to do this team, set in the future, and you'll get something brilliant. The original Guardians are amazing and they deserve another chance in the sun.

I'm an older fan. Back in the day, the library down the road from my house had Marvel books. They were mostly New Universe comics, so well-printed toilet paper for the most part, but they also had two books that would go down as some of my favorites – X-Factor (Vol. 1) and New Warriors (Vol. 1). The '90s were the thirtieth anniversary of the Silver Age Marvel Universe and the publisher was going out of their way to highlight this and create a new breed of heroes. The New Warriors were meant to be the modern equivalent of those classic teams, an all-new group of heroes that would form the next generation of the Marvel Universe.

Night Thrasher, Speedball, Nova, Namorita, Marvel Boy/Justice, and Firestar made a splash right away, thanks to the brilliant creative team of Fabian Nicieza and Mark Bagley. However, despite that strong start, they would never reach their promised position as the next generation of heroes and since then no one has even tried to make it happen. The New Warriors is an excellent group, full of cool heroes, and they are exactly what Marvel needs. The last time Marvel talked about bringing them back, they were able to anger both sides of the political divide, so this time, they should play them straight – what happens when the next big thing fails? The New Warriors have so much potential and it's about time they reached it (I can work up a pitch in about a day, Marvel).

The Avengers are Marvel's greatest team , leading the publisher to create new versions of the group. The first time was the premiere of the West Coast Avengers, giving the western half of the United States their own superheroes. Eventually, someone at the company decided to take this idea – a group of heroes protecting a particular geographic area – and play it for laughs. Thus, the Great Lakes Avengers were born. The team was meant to protect the Great Lakes region, a major commerce corridor for both the United States and Canada, but the members of the team were basically the not-quite ready for primetime players.

The group consisted of Mr. Immortal, Big Bertha, Doorman, Dinah Soar, and Flatman, each of them with powers that could be cool, but were just ridiculous enough. They were the joke team and their return in the mid '00s GLA: Misassembled (a title meant to lampoon both JLA and "Avengers Disassembled") helped make Dan Slott into a hot creator and was the first major return of Squirrel Girl. The Great Lakes Avengers are a team that is perfect for this age of Internet humor and Marvel should be trying to figure out a way to make them work (sadly, I don't have a pitch for this one).

Marvel has two Canada adjacent superteams, which isn't that weird, but still strange that it has two of them it does nothing with, especially with the amount of Canadian creators they have under contract. Alpha Flight was created by Chris Claremont and John Byrne, serving as an important part of Wolverine's history. They were the superhero arm of Department H, the secret Canadian organization that was charged with protecting the Great White North from superhuman threats. The first volume of Alpha Flight ran for 11 years and a 130 issues, becoming a rather beloved part of the Marvel Universe.

The team of Canadian heroes – Guardian, Vindicator, Sasquatch, Shaman, Box, Snowbird, Northstar, Aurora, and Marrina – have gone through numerous permutations over the years, with its latest role being an international superteam based in space, defending the Earth. However, Marvel needs to just go back to basics, bring back the Canadian government team, and let them have adventures. There's so much that can be done with them and it's about time they got another chance to shine.

The X-Men first debuted as a teen team, but they didn't really catch on. The second, older version of the team did, but eventually, Marvel wanted to try a teen mutant team again. This led to New Mutants , a book that became a beloved part of X-history and introduced the next generation of mutants. It would turn into X-Force , which was the young adult team, leaving the House of Ideas in need of a new group of teen mutants for the '90s. This led to the creation of Generation X , the group headlined by Jubilee, Emma Frost, and Banshee.

The team consisted of mutants with bizarre powers like Chamber, Husk, Skin, Penance, Mondo, and M, something of a commentary on teen culture of the team (if you were there, you'd understand; the '90s were when alternative culture became mainstream). The book's quirky art style from Chris Bachalo and Mark Buckingham turned heads and it became a rather beloved, if a tad bit niche, mutant book. They faded away in the early '00s before a reboot in 2017 that was great, but I'm pretty sure I was the only reading. The X-Men are doing good, but if Marvel could nail a new Generation X, things would be even better.

What Marvel teams do you think deserve a major comeback? Do you think they could help Marvel turn the tides? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Box Office: 'Sunrise on the Reaping' Reignites 'Hunger Games' Franchise With $120 Million Debut
articles.summary: "Sunrise on the Reaping" caught fire at the domestic box office, collecting a sensational $120 million in its opening weekend while reinvigorating Lionsgate's "Hunger Games" franchise. Overseas, "Sunrise on the Reaping" generated $105 million from 84 territories for a towering launch of $225 million globally. The dystopian prequel is one of just five movies this […]
articles.content:
"Sunrise on the Reaping" caught fire at the domestic box office, collecting a sensational $120 million in its opening weekend while reinvigorating Lionsgate's "Hunger Games" franchise.

The dystopian prequel is one of just five movies this year to launch above $100 million, joining the company of "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" ($360 million), “Toy Story 5” ($159 million), “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” ($131 million) and “The Odyssey” ($123 million). All of those films eventually surpassed the $1 billion mark globally. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support

“‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ posting an impressive $100 million-plus debut reinforces just how vital 'The Hunger Games' remains as a movie franchise,” says Paul Dergarabedian, Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" coincided with another big release — albeit not at the movies. Rockstar’s video game “Grand Theft Auto VI" launched after years of anticipation, earning a staggering $3.79 billion on its first day . It's expected to set a sales record for entertainment across any medium.

“Many have speculated as to whether the release of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ would hurt ‘The Hunger Game’ at the box office, and I think the marketplace has already spoken," adds Dergarabedian. “There’s plenty of time to play ‘GTA VI’ and make it to a theater to see ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ this weekend."

On top of pitched competition at home, initial ticket sales for "Sunrise on the Reaping" are notable because they're not far off from original saga. For reference, 2012’s “The Hunger Games” ignited to $152 million, followed by 2013’s “Catching Fire” ($158 million), 2014’s “Mockingjay Part 1” ($121 million) and 2015’s “Mockingjay Part 2” ($102 million). Nearly a decade after those movies, starring Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson, concluded their run, the studio revived the young-adult property with 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes," an origin story about Panem's cruel leader, President Coriolanus Snow. That film, set during the 10th Hunger Games, bowed significantly below its predecessors with $44 million. However, the movie stuck around through the holidays and eventually climbed to $363 million globally, registering as a win against a (comparatively leaner) $100 million budget and justifying another prequel for the studio. "Sunrise on the Reaping," which returns to Panem for the 50th Hunger Games, carries a larger price tag above $150 million, not including the many millions spent on worldwide marketing efforts. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That "Sunrise on the Reaping" managed to recapture the spark of the initial series is impressive as the sixth installment in any property. And the film earned a strong "A-" grade on CinemaScore exit polls, which bodes well for box office longevity. Analysts attribute the strong debut to several factors, including the franchise's multi-generational appeal as well as the excitement for the return of fan-favorite characters. This chapter, based on the novel by Suzanne Collins, has a stronger connection to the original saga; the story follows a young Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada takes on the role originally played by Woody Harrelson) — who eventually mentors Katniss (Lawrence) and Peeta (Hutcherson) in their Hunger Games, a Battle Royale for teens. Francis Lawrence returned to direct, having helmed all but the first chapter in the YA-centric franchise.

"The last 'Hunger Games' stumbled when the story went back 64 years without Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson," says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. "This is a strong return."

"Sunrise on the Reaping" is Lionsgate's second major theatrical victory in 2026 following "Michael," which captured a huge $97 million in its debut and became the first biopic ever to cross the $1 billion mark. With this weekend's haul, "The Hunger Games" series has collectively generated $3.43 billion in global ticket sales to stand as the studio's highest-grossing franchise ever, above "The Twilight Saga" ($3.3 billion worldwide across five films).

Second place went to “ I Play Rocky ” earned $9.3 million while expanding nationwide to 2,477 theaters. The Amazon MGM movie, which depicts the real-life story of Sylvester Stallone bringing the 1976 classic “Rocky” to the big screen, has generated $10.4 million after two weekends in limited release. Audiences, roughly half were over 45 years old, awarded the feel-good film a rare "A+" grade on CinemaScore. "I Play Rocky," which hopes to find itself in the Oscar race, cost about $30 million to produce.

Last weekend's champ "Ebenezer" dropped to third place with $7.7 million from 3,545 venues, a steep 60% decline from its opening. Paramount's PG-13 take on "A Christmas Carol," starring Johnny Depp in his first major Hollywood role in eight years, has generated $32.5 million in North America and $78 million globally. It's not quite a resounding embrace of Depp amid the actor's return to studio fare. However it'll be decently positioned in its theatrical run against a modest $38 million budget. (Theater owners keep half of ticket sales.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In limited release, the Focus Features drama "Elsinore" earned $240,000 from six locations in New York and Los Angeles, translating to $40,000 per theater. To compare, another awards hopeful, A24's drama "Club Kid" had a $65,097 per-screen-average from six venues, while "I Play Rocky" averaged $49,200 per location in its initial frame. "Elsinore" stars Andrew Scott as the Scottish actor Ian Charleson who secretly battles AIDS while playing "Hamlet" in London. Focus will continue to roll out the film through December.

“Sunrise on the Reaping” provided a nice jolt to the box office ahead of Thanksgiving. This Turkey Day might not cement any theatrical records, but the holiday should be busy for theater owners. "Hunger Games" will continue to draw crowds alongside new offerings like Universal’s comedy “Focker in Law,” with Ariana Grande joining Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro, Disney’s animated “Hexed” and Netflix’s Imax release of “The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.”

"This is a very good weekend," Gross says. "The weekend before Thanksgiving sets up 10 very strong days. Moviegoing is back on track."

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One Piece 's live-action series is fast approaching its return to Netflix next year, and it's one step closer to that launch with the start of a new wave of behind-the-scenes videos showing off more of the series' production. One Piece has been an incredible success for Netflix ever since the live-action series first made its debut . Quickly renewed for not just one, but two new seasons, the team behind it all has been hard at work on adapting Eiichiro Oda's massive manga series for the past few years.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta is the third major season of the live-action series as it sees Luffy and the Straw Hats heading into Alabasta in order to save Princess Vivi's kingdom , but it has yet to confirm a proper release date as of this time. But now that seems closer than ever before as One Piece will begin to release a series of special behind the scenes videos to give fans a better look at how Season 2 all came together. It's time to get hyped.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta is currently scheduled for a release with Netflix sometime in 2027 , but has yet to nail down a more concrete release date or window as of this time. This new wave of behind the scenes videos for the second season kick off a new project that will likely lead to the reveal of when this third season is finally coming our way. With promotional materials for the franchise heating up once more, it's time to start looking ahead to what could be coming our way in this new season.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta will be expanding its roles for some of the major players who debuted in the second season such as Mikaela Hoover as Tony Tony Chopper, Charithra Chandran as Princess Vivi, Sendhil Ramamurthy as Nefartari Cobra, Lera Abova as Nico Robin, and Joe Manganiello as Sir Crocodile ( who has been steadily teasing his return for the past few months as well ). Serving as the Straw Hats' first major battle on the Grand Line, this could be a major turning point for the franchise.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta will also be introducing many new faces to the expanding cast with the introduction of this new region too such as Xolo Maridueña as Ace , Cole Escola as Bon Clay, Awdo Awdo as Mr. 1, Daisy Head as Miss Doublefinger, Emilio Sakraya as Koza, Omid Abtahi as Toto, Jamie Ward as Pell, and Nabeel Khan as Chaka revealed thus far. But there will likely be many other new faces revealed the closer we get to Season 3's big debut in the coming months.

With the franchise revealing more behind the scenes information for the second season, it's going to give fans the best look yet at how production has been thinking in their approach to it all. This is going to be very important heading into the third season as the future of the live-action series remains uncertain , but we'll have to see how it shakes out soon enough. But what do you want to see from One Piece 's live-action series next? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A remaster of an entire and iconic PS1 trilogy of games is now available for $2.54. This is less than $1 per game and is unsurprisingly the cheapest the remastered trilogy has ever been available. While the games in question are PlayStation games from yesteryear, this new deal does not come via the PlayStation Store, but via Fanatical, which has Steam codes available at this price until December 1.

More precisely, until December 1, Fanatical is giving out Steam codes for Tomb Raider I-III Remastered available for $2.54. This is a 2024 collection that features remasters of 1996's Tomb Raider , 1997's Tomb Raider II , and 1998's Tomb Raider III , all from Core Design, the original developer behind the series before Crystal Dynamics took over. Whether these are the best Tomb Raider trilogy in the series is debatable, but it is certainly the most iconic, and an absolute steal at $2.54. That said, PC users may already own these games because they were given away for free on Epic Games Store earlier this year .

As you may know, the second and third of these Tomb Raider games are notably PS1 console exclusives. The first game, though, was actually a Sega Saturn exclusive at launch, before coming to other platforms, including the PS1.

Good, But Not Great Remasters Upon release in 2024, Tomb Raider I-III Remastered from Aspyr earned a 71 to 75 Metacritic range, which isn't great, but it's not bad either. It's decent. That said, its user review score on Steam is actually a bit higher than this, with 83% of Steam user reviews rating the game positively.

Positives of the remastered collection are how faithful they are, and that they include the expansions rather than lock them behind a separate purchase. The graphics are also appreciably improved. Unfortunately, the controls of the games weren't appreciably improved, and the bad news is the controls of the PS1 originals don't hold up well. The camera also isn't very good, and there is a lack of modern quality-of-life features, such as autosaves. To this end, the remaster makes revisiting the PS1 games much easier in 2026; however, they don't modernize the games enough for first-time visitors. In other words, while nostalgia is not required, it is recommened.

Those who end up checking out these nostalgic action-adventure games from yesteryear should expect to fork over at least 40 hours to see the trilogy through from start to finish. Completionists, meanwhile, will need roughly 90 hours with the Lara Croft games.

If this PS1 deal does not tickle your fancy, there is another great PS1 deal right now, and this one is available via the PlayStation Store, where a PS1 classic from 1997 has been discounted to $2.39 .

articles.title: Netflix's The Body Isn't Like My Catholic School Experience, But It Gives Me Flashbacks
articles.summary: As wild as it is to admit, I resonated with this.
articles.content:
The Body is available to stream right now with a Netflix subscription , and when I learned it was about controversy surrounding a Catholic school, I had to check it out. As someone who attended a Catholic grade school and high school, I was eager to see how it was portrayed, and while things were a bit wilder than I remember, the show really nailed two parts.

Project Hail Mary was called " blatant Catholic propaganda ," as described by someone who never watched, and similarly, The Body is being vilified by groups of concerned Catholics who have not and likely will not watch it. As someone who did, I'll admit no one should go into this assuming it'll be a family-friendly adventure, but the parts that handle religion are done with lots of care.

I also think The Body does a great job of handling what goes down when something controversial does happen at a Catholic school. I can't get into specifics, but there was a controversy at my school so big that it received national attention, and the fact that it was a Catholic school only amplified the interest and headlines.

Like the kids in The Body , a number of kids attending were from families of some renown. Families were willing to keep quiet about events occurring to protect their children, and the school was eager to let any controversy fade as quickly as possible.

articles.title: Wait, How Many People Left Can Actually Win Survivor 51?
articles.summary: Seriously, what is going on with this season?
articles.content:
I’m not sure if you’ve noticed, but Survivor 51 is running out of main characters . We’ve somehow lost four of the biggest, loudest and most vibrant personalities in consecutive weeks, and now, we’re suddenly left with a season that has a few main characters, a couple wacky side characters and a bunch of people who have been consistently deprioritized and underedited throughout the season. What is going on? How many of these castaways can actually even win?

I’m not saying the person who wins every season is the person with the most confessionals or the person with the most sympathetic edit, but one recurring theme is that the winner is always a consistent and active part of the narrative. The show goes out of their way to give us their perspective on what’s going on because the ultimate payoff needs to feel earned and it needs to make sense. That’s just storytelling 101. If we want to know, for example, why someone on the jury does or doesn’t vote for them at the end, it helps if we’re given context and confessionals about their relationship.

Mike and Eric have been much more present parts of the edit, but their storylines have both been about how much everyone else is annoyed with them. Eric has been getting a wacky theater kid edit that has included multiple montages of him talking and everyone else being annoyed by it . There have maybe been ten shots of characters literally rolling their eyes after he talks. Mike is a different version of the same situation. He’s been the subject of numerous confessionals from other players about how he’s a “bottom feeder” and impossible to work with. I don’t see why Survivor would portray its winner that way.

articles.title: Two Different Xbox Consoles Released On The Same Day, But Their Impacts Couldn't Be More Different
articles.summary: Courtesy of Microsoft The Xbox console series has released two systems on November 22nd, once in 2005 with the highly celebrated Xbox 360 and again in 2013 with the more controversial Xbox One. While definitely a marketing strategy that didn't apply to the 2020 launch of the current Xbox Series X|S console on November 10th, the last two […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Xbox console series has released two systems on November 22nd, once in 2005 with the highly celebrated Xbox 360 and again in 2013 with the more controversial Xbox One. While definitely a marketing strategy that didn't apply to the 2020 launch of the current Xbox Series X|S console on November 10th, the last two devices in the Xbox line-up couldn't have been received more differently by audiences. In many ways, the lasting legacy of the Xbox 360 and Xbox One represent the highs and lows of Xbox as a gaming company, with their mistakes from both eras still existing as something players feel today.

The next Xbox console is currently called "Project Helix" according to internal sources, with predictions estimating that it could come out around the 2027 or 2028 holiday season. With Xbox laying off over 3,000 employees in their gaming division during a massive "reset" of the company, the 2028 date is far more likely as studios close down and scrutiny of Xbox is higher than ever before. Industry trends such as the skyrocketing costs of manufacturing parts of any electronic device will also play a key part in Project Helix's release, marking a much different atmosphere to the Xbox 360 and Xbox One's time in the sun.

The time periods of gaming when the Xbox 360 and Xbox One released couldn't be more different, with each marking a different kind of evolution of console quality and exclusivity. Microsoft likely released the Xbox One on the same day as the 360 once did due to the former console's celebrated status, as it still remains one of the most influential home systems in the industry to this day. Without the Xbox 360, the modern landscape of online play simply wouldn't exist, from Xbox Live and Xbox Game Pass to PlayStation+, Nintendo Online, and similar features. Across eight years, the Xbox 360 became a gaming cornerstone for a variety of reasons.

At the time, the Xbox 360 was widely considered much better than even the Nintendo Wii, whose strange motion control systems were associated more with family or party games. Meanwhile, the PlayStation 3 was lacking the innovations of the Xbox 360 when it came to accessibility and quality-of-life, making it feel like another version of the PS2 rather than something new. While PlayStation 3 games were better by comparison, the compact controller of the Xbox 360 was almost perfect, setting a standard other consoles have tried to follow years later. For that reason, it's no wonder why the Xbox One wanted to capture that nostalgia by following the 360's release date.

The beginning of the Xbox 360's reign is hardly as celebrated as you might think by the time the console's life cycle ended, mainly due to one infamous hardware problem. The "red ring of death" was an issue for the earliest version of the Xbox 360, where players' entire consoles bricked after a red ring showed up on their power button. This caused tons of recalls, refunds, or big wastes of money of some fans' parts, leading to massive frustration around the console. However, this didn't take away from the easier time developers had actually making games that appeared on the console itself.

The really easy controller design (both in style and connectivity) helped any player become familiar with the Xbox 360 in some way, with standout games like Halo: Reach , Gears of War , and Forza being great exclusives on the console too. The hardware eventually became reliable enough to host large multiplayer groups, creating LAN parties for games like Halo 3 that are legendary among players who remember that era. Speaking of multiplayer, the Xbox 360 was revolutionary in the way that it pioneered online functionality, allowing players to engage in a variety of social features other consoles simply didn't have.

For example, the Xbox 360 allowed groups of players to add each other as friends in an online ecosystem, which in turn set up online messaging chat rooms for better communication. Players could jump into party calls as a whole group or just with one individual friend, primarily to coordinate jumping into a specific game together for multiplayer experiences. Unique profiles through gamertags helped players establish online identities here too, creating social circles that created lasting memories for years to come.

By contrast, the Xbox One was leagues below the Xbox 360 in terms of overall impact. While the Xbox 360 didn't have to compete much against other consoles, the Xbox One had to deal with the PlayStation 4, which was a far more robust device with a greater number of high-quality exclusives. Everything from Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man , the new Norse God of War games, and other great titles that didn't appear on the Xbox One at all, making the console feel like it was a step behind. However, games weren't the only reason the Xbox One failed, as business practices surrounding it also put it at a disadvantage.

The Xbox One released during a time when the console was extremely overpriced compared to other consoles on the market, being sold as a "complete entertainment system" for movies, TV, and streaming alongside games. The multimedia approach wasn't necessarily a bad thing in the long run, as new consoles like the PS5 have that setup now. For the time, though, the Xbox One's price didn't justify that strategy, especially when players figured out the console was planning on having daily online checks and a lending of physical games rather than ownership of them. Long before the PS5 announced the end of physical game production, the Xbox One was doing it first.

Higher pricing also applied to the Xbox One's strange side piece of hardware — the Xbox Kinect. The Kinect was a strange way Microsoft was trying to compete with Nintendo, mimicking the Nintendo Wii's motion control systems with voice activated commands and players' physical actions being mapped to the games they played. Needless to say, this was not the right move, often leading to glitches and strange games that players had to pay hundreds of dollars for. This also started Microsoft's era to buy up various game studios at seemingly random, while not putting out any great exclusives that helped sell the console as part of those partnerships.

Constant struggles to create first-party games is ultimately what sank the Xbox One, even if players praised the Xbox Game Pass library that offered game catalogs for a subscription price. Weaker hardware options and damaged player trust caused many people to switch to the PS4, and even more to the Nintendo Switch when it eventually released during the Xbox One's time. While the Xbox Series X|S is a step in the right direction, the missteps of the Xbox One are a shame, as the evergreen popularity of the Xbox 360 once marked Microsoft as on top of the competition before its big collapse.

What Xbox console do you have the most memories with? Let us know in the comments below!

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Another major series has ended its run in the pages of Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine after six years of serialization with the release of its final chapter, and it makes the 14th title coming to an end this year overall. It's the final transitional phase for Shonen Jump for the year as a final batch of series are coming to their ends, and a few new titles are kicking off their own runs. And following the end of Kenta Shinohara's Witch Watch last week , Yuto Suzuki's Sakamoto Days has now come to an end.

Yuto Suzuki's Sakamoto Days has now officially come to an end with Shonen Jump with the release of Chapter 284, six years after it originally made its debut. The series has been in the midst of its final arc for the past year, so fans have been preparing to say goodbye to the series for quite some time. But with many more fans assuming it would end earlier this Summer, the story was able to take its time and reach a more conclusive finale than many other Shonen Jump titles get .

Sakamoto Days comes to an end with the release of Chapter 284 , and the series puts a final stamp on Taro Sakamoto's journey overall. Following the final fight with X, the penultimate chapter of the series moved time ahead a year or so to the birth of the Sakamoto family's next child. With the JAA being dismantled and assassins no longer being needed, Sakamoto starts a whole new group to take its place that uses non-lethal tactics for its takedowns instead in order to keep the power balance.

Sakamoto's dream of turning his convenience store into a franchise has also worked with a chain of stores across the region, and the final chapter reveals how each of the survivors (both friends and former foes) have since gone on to live new lives that don't focus on killing. It's a bright future for everyone as the world finds a new era of peace after everything that's happened, and it's clear that Sakamoto has indeed had an impact on everyone he's come across through his time as a deadly killer.

Though Sakamoto Days has now come to an end, thankfully it's far from the end of the franchise on a whole. The anime is set to return to screens with Season 2 in January , and it's already looking to keep up the hot streak. As for Shonen Jump , this is the 14th major title to come to an end this year but only the sixth series to end under its own terms without being cancelled. The number of titles that have ended in 2026 break down as such:

With one new series still scheduled to make its debut next week following the return of two major creators that have started off their own new works , it likely means there will be one more series ended before 2026 comes to an end. But how are you feeling about Sakamoto Days coming to an end? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: 5 Animated Movies That Struggled Because Everyone Thought They Were Just For Kids
articles.summary: Animation has given us many classic movies over the years. Naturally, the name Disney is one of the first evoked by any mention of the genre, but there are several other movie studios that have built remarkable reputations for success off the back of their animated films. Pixar, DreamWorks, Studio Ghibli — some of the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Animation has given us many classic movies over the years. Naturally, the name Disney is one of the first evoked by any mention of the genre, but there are several other movie studios that have built remarkable reputations for success off the back of their animated films. Pixar, DreamWorks, Studio Ghibli — some of the best animated movies ever made have come from various different studios and filmmakers. Considering the genre built its success on family-friendly fare, it's perhaps unsurprising that this is the most common perception of its movies: that they're mostly just for kids. However, that stance dismisses and diminishes the quality of some truly exceptional films.

Throughout the genre's history, there have been many great animated movies that are all too quickly dismissed by general audiences. The perception that animated films only have something to offer to the youngest members of their audiences is the sort of rash, sweeping generalization that glosses over some truly great movies. Each of the following is an exceptional film that also happens to be animated, but the notion that they were made just for kids ultimately hurt their chances for the success they deserved.

The Iron Giant is fondly remembered today by the many '90s kids who were emotionally traumatized by it upon its original release. Brad Bird's 1999 movie told the story of a young boy who befriends a huge, alien robot, set against the backdrop of a particularly paranoid 1950s America. The Cold War subtext was naturally lost on many of the movie's younger audience members, but most adults were quick to dismiss the movie due to its animation style, which evoked the Disney movies of the era. This led to the awesome sci-fi movie being a box office flop in spite of its incredible quality.

In the years since, the brilliance of The Iron Giant has been more widely recognized, but that doesn't do anything to change its lack of initial success. The movie's deeper narrative themes and emotional weight gave it many qualities that only older viewers could truly appreciate, and it has since come to be considered one of the best animated movies of its time. The idea that The Iron Giant was just for kids might have since been dispelled, but that can never change the fact that the movie struggled at the box office as a result of that misguided perception.

Atlantis: The Lost Empire was released during an incredibly interesting period of Disney animation. After spending the 1990s making the animated musicals that are most commonly associated with the studio, 2001 saw them try something decidedly different with an animated adventure movie inspired by classic pulp fiction and the sci-fi works of writers such as Jules Verne. Unfortunately, Disney underestimated just how much their movies were perceived as being specifically for kids, and Atlantis: The Lost Empire struggled as a result.

Now remembered as one of Disney's most underrated movies , Atlantis: The Lost Empire has come to be considered a cult classic. However, the scope of its fantastical sci-fi adventure was something that, as well as being one of Disney's most ambitious experiments, deserved to secure a much wider audience. Sadly, the Disney label, combined with marketing that failed to communicate the movie's universal appeal, saw Atlantis dismissed as just another kids movie for far too long.

Titan A.E. is perhaps the most obscure title on this list, but it's probably also the one with the biggest cult following. The year 2000 saw Don Bluth turn his hand to making a sprawling space opera using the animation techniques that had seen him deliver numerous successful movies, resulting in Titan A.E ., an animated movie with a cast packed with huge Hollywood stars . Its story followed Cale Tucker, a young man in the 31st century tasked with protecting a giant spaceship that could save humanity after the destruction of Earth.

Despite the strength of its epic sci-fi premise, Titan A.E. was unable to secure the success or attention it deserved. The style of its animation led to many people dismissing it as another adventure movie made for kids, but the level of violence and the complexities of its plot meant that it also struggled to appeal to young children. This unfortunately led to the movie becoming a box office bomb that effectively killed Fox Animation Studios, which is especially tragic considering just how excellent Titan A.E. actually is.

There are a handful of Disney box office failures that eventually became fan-favorite movies , but none as well-known as Treasure Planet . A particularly ambitious adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson's literary classic Treasure Island , the movie sought to transplant its story into outer space. A breathtaking combination of traditional hand-drawn animation and computer-generated imagery, Treasure Planet remains one of Disney's most original adaptations of a previously existing story, and has since come to be considered one of the best animated movies of the 2000s.

Treasure Planet 's underwhelming marketing campaign did nothing to help dispel the notion that it was purely for children. Its appeal wasn't at all communicated by promotional material, with adults who would have enjoyed its sci-fi reimagining of a familiar story instead seeing it as just another animated Disney movie. This was one of the major factors in the movie becoming a financial disappointment, and while Treasure Planet proved to be one of the best Disney movies of all time, it took years to build that reputation because of how it was initially dismissed by so many.

Shane Acker's 9 is one of the strangest and most interesting animated movies of the 21st century so far. The post-apocalyptic sci-fi story is set in an alternate version of the 1940s and follows the titular rag doll who awakens shortly after the uprising of machines, which in turn led to the eradication of humanity. The only resistance against the machines is the rag doll Stitchpunks, setting a particularly bleak backdrop for the animated movie. Perhaps unsurprisingly, 9 struggled to find its audience.

Many thought the film seemed too dark for young children, but a lot of older audiences saw the animated movie as being aimed at another demographic. Existing in this liminal space between the two, 9 's brilliance wasn't recognized widely enough, and it passed into relative obscurity. With the movie's potential sequel seeming destined to go unmade, it is now remembered as a great standalone animated movie that deserved much greater success. It's now clear that it was never truly intended for a particularly young audience, but that its distinct visual identity and complex premise should have been better targeted at more mature viewers.

articles.title: GTA 6 Features an Unexpected Connection to Red Dead Redemption 2
articles.summary: The newest Grand Theft Auto game from Rockstar Games features an unexpected connection to Red Dead Redemption 2. While the poor Metacritic user review score has derailed the perfect launch for GTA 6, Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, won't mind because it's the biggest entertainment release in history, and it's not even […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The newest Grand Theft Auto game from Rockstar Games features an unexpected connection to Red Dead Redemption 2 . While the poor Metacritic user review score has derailed the perfect launch for GTA 6 , Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, won't mind because it's the biggest entertainment release in history , and it's not even close. It is also the highest-rated video game with critics of all time as well.

Whether it's the greatest game of all time is up for debate, but it arguably has the best case. Another game with a great case is Red Dead Redemption 2 , Rockstar Games' previous newest release. And these two games have an unexpected connection, confirmed by Cali Elizabeth Moore. For those who do not recognize this name, this is the actress who plays Abigail Roberts in Red Dead Redemption 2 and its predecessor.

The RDR2 actress is not in GTA 6 in any capacity. She has no role in the game, but she did have a role in making the game. It's been revealed that the actress served as casting director for GTA 6 . To this end, if you love or hate the casting in the new Grand Theft Auto game, you owe it to Moore. While this was a new role for Moore, Rockstar Games didn't really deviate from its mantra of largely using acting talent with minimal to no experience working on games. And in the grand scheme of things, relatively unknown talent compared to the Hollywood stars it could certainly attract to the roles.

According to Moore, she cast "thousands and thousands of actors all over the world" for the game. It is unclear what years this work happened in and whether she is still working for the studio. Whatever the case, she ran casting for it all, from the main characters to the random strippers in the game.

"After years of casting thousands and thousands of actors all over the world for this project, I am so proud of what my amazing team has accomplished," writes Moore in the Instagram post above. "Spending countless hours finding an actor fluent in the right accent of Spanish, a stripper for the right strip club animation, an actor worthy of our brilliantly written main characters, a stunt performer to execute a jaw-dropping stunt, the perfect authentic face for a scan, it was a huge task and it feels so good to share this work with the world."

Grand Theft Auto VI is available via PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S, and Xbox Series X. What lies ahead for the game and Rockstar Games, remains to be seen, but according to a new report, its next game is not a GTA game nor a Red Dead Redemption game .

articles.title: Minutes Before Macaulay Culkin’s Home Alone Sequel News, The OG Director Said It Couldn’t Happen
articles.summary: A bit of awkward timing, but the filmmaker makes some good points.
articles.content:
I can't imagine Home Alone fans expected this much Kevin McCallister news ahead of Thanksgiving. Macaulay Culkin is reportedly returning to act in the franchise that made him a household name. But just minutes before that story hit amid the 2026 movie calendar , Chris Columbus, the director of the first two movies, was explaining why he didn't think another sequel could happen. And Columbus has a pretty heartbreaking reason for that.

He's got a point. We all remember Kevin setting traps for Harry and Marv, screaming after putting on aftershave and eating a ridiculous amount of ice cream. But the first film also follows a frantic mother trying to get back to the child she accidentally left behind. That film's final reunion is still one of my favorite parts, and the late Catherine O'Hara , who played Kevin's mother, Kate McCallister, is at least 50% of why it works so well. O'Hara died in January at 71, and Columbus believes her absence would be impossible to overcome. As he explained:

Unfortunately, the reunion he pictured is no longer possible. That makes the timing of his interview particularly surreal. He continued:

As essential as O’Hara was to the success of the first two movies, the bumbling baddies also made the film unforgettable. I'm, of course, talking about the Wet Bandits, played by Daniel Stern and Joe Pesci . Columbus also wanted to make sure those two other actors got their due, adding:

I can’t argue with the longtime filmmaker. The subsequent installments have struggled to reproduce the burglars' chemistry. Persci and Stern are hilarious in these iconic roles and not one single actor in any of the follow-up movies holds a candle to their performances in both of the first two movies. Getting hit in the face with a paint can is only funny so many times, but those two made it an art form.

After Columbus directed 1990's Home Alone and 1992's Home Alone 2: Lost in New York , the series continued without Culkin in Home Alone 3 , Home Alone 4 , Home Alone: The Holiday Heist and 2021's Home Sweet Home Alone . None brought back the core pairing that Columbus considers essential, and you can feel their absence.

As for the new project, there's an interesting idea on the table. During a fan event in 2025, Culkin floated a potential sequel in which an adult Kevin is raising a son who locks him out of the house and turns his father's old tricks against him. Reports suggest the film could follow Kevin's perspective as a dad, although no final story or additional casting has been confirmed.

articles.title: GTA 6 - How To Improve Your Health & Stats Fast, Explained
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games Physical health in Grand Theft Auto 6 is an underrated feature in the game, determining both Jason and Lucia's stats at times in both positive in negative ways. Should you eat junk food and live a sedentary life, your stats could fall off, causing either character to be weaker in gameplay as a result. Different […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Physical health in Grand Theft Auto 6 is an underrated feature in the game, determining both Jason and Lucia's stats at times in both positive in negative ways. Should you eat junk food and live a sedentary life, your stats could fall off, causing either character to be weaker in gameplay as a result. Different activities can do the opposite, making your character strong by improving their health, causing other stats to grow and act as the main strategies for "leveling up" Lucia or Jason throughout GTA 6 's story Chapters.

Stamina is one of the most important stats in GTA 6 , and it is directly impacted by the attention you put on Jason or Lucia's health as the days go by in-game. There are some obvious answers to increasing Stamina, like working out using your phone's fitness app, but there are more subtle options scattered within the game that can actually bring you to a healthy status much faster than you'd think. The overwhelming details in GTA 6 give players nearly endless ways to interact with the world, including how they choose to pursue physical actions that provide clear gameplay bonuses.

Your health and Stamina in GTA 6 are easily improved by a solid workout, or any sort of physical action that is listed as such within the game through a heart or lightning symbol. Should these icons appear, you know that whatever you're about to do has a direct health benefit, leading to better stats despite being completely optional. The fitness app on your phone will list your character's physical stat values, represented by the three stats listed below:

Other stats are tied to physical health too, such as a character's generally Strength. Jason and Lucia have separate stats, so working out with one character won't raise scores for another. This limitation means you have to find some strategies to increase stats fast, to raise each of the three listed beyond the upgrade points built within them. Stamina, Focus, and Health all have a maximum Level of 4, with players gathering "experience" through activities to reach each Level eventually. That being said, you can't just work out continuously until you max out everything, as you have to pace out your physical improvement.

Players are unable to gain more than 33% progress in any of the three physical stat categories in a single day, marking a big obstacle to overcome. Basically, you can do three cardio or strength workouts in a row to reach this level before the game prevents you from doing any more. It takes around one in-game day for the workout window to reopen, unless you are using some sort of cheats in GTA 6 to get around this. To make matters more difficult, you only have a four day window to work out, meaning you have to schedule times to improve fitness rather than just doing it whenever you want.

There are ways to skip past the workout timer in GTA 6 , letting you increase stats again without having to wait as long. Consuming in-game items like protein shakes, coffee, or a protein bar knock the one-day workout timer down to a half-day, and even more depending on how much you eat or drink. Obviously, there's a limit here too, but if you are trying to fit as much exercise into a four-day workout window as possible, this is a good way of ensuring Jason and Lucia have the chance to do that. Getting a healthy routine can help you farm stat increases fast, as long as you know what activities to do.

Drinking, sleeping, showering, and maintaining other physical health traits will also reduce the workout timer, opening up other opportunities to increase Stamina, Focus, or Health stats. Look for a green lightning bolt on certain activities to do this, in the same way you would see that symbol on food or drink items. Some items in GTA 6 even give Lucia or Jason temporary buffs to physical stats for a short time, which can be good before big missions or story events. Normal gameplay can also do this, but paying attention to the activities that do this best will make sure your stats grow constantly.

Cardio and strength training increase Stamina and Health respectively, either through specific workouts or various activities out in the world. For example, running or swimming around will eventually improve your Stamina score, helping it reach different Levels the more you do. That being said, you have to gradually increase the challenge of your stat-growing activities for them to keep being effective, otherwise you'll see less results. This means that if you want to improve Health by lifting weights, you have to lift heavier and heavier weights to get the same boosts to the stat as you were seeing in the beginning.

However, Focus works in a totally different way than Stamina or Health, as the same activities that improve those scores do nothing for this mental stat. You have to do actions that require concentration to improve Focus, such as going to shooting ranges or meditating at home. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The saga of the DCU is one of the most frustrating in superhero history. James Gunn and Peter Safran were brought in to head DC Studios and many fans were excited. Peacemaker, Creature Commandos, and Superman were all varying degrees of successful, Lanterns was one of the highest rated shows on HBO Max, Clayface had a respectable run, but Supergirl underperformed and that's become the story of the nascent superhero universe. Warner Brothers Discovery was sold to SkyDance, Gunn and Safran are out, and former MCU producer Jeremy Latcham is in. Latcham did some interviews, implying that he wanted to take the DCU in a more family-friendly direction. Luckily for him, DC Comics has plenty of wholesome heroes, including the first superteam: the Justice Society of America .

SkyDance is a company run by conservative billionaires and there are many who assume that the changes to DC Studios are for this reason. The DCU was a little more risque than the MCU, though, so there is something to making more family-friendly movies and that's why the new DC Studios needs to focus on the Justice Society. Not only are they the most important superteam ever – the none of the rest would exist without them – but family has always played an important role in the history of the group.

So, it all started with Superman. He was a smash hit and more heroes started popping up – Batman, Wonder Woman, Hawkman, Green Lantern, Dr. Fate, Flash, Hawkman, Wildcat, the Atom, the Sandman, Mr. Terrific, Doctor Mid-Nite, Johnny Thunder – and eventually DC would decide that if one hero was great, a group of them would be better. Justice Society comics back then were very different – they were basically anthology books, with each member of the team getting their own chapter. Fans loved getting team stories, and soon more and more characters started to pop up, leading to the creation of the All-Star Squadron, as the teams fought Nazis and their allies.

The Justice Society faded away in the '50s, but would return in the '60s with the introduction of Earth-Two. Since then, the Justice Society have starred in amazing stories , becoming one of the most beloved teams ever. One of the most important factors in the team's success is legacy. The team began to bring in their children, training them to be heroes, just as younger heroes took up empty mantles. The core of the Justice Society – the surviving Golden Age members like Green Lantern, Flash, Hawkman, Hawkgirl, and Wildcat – have taken it upon themselves to teach the next generation of heroes the game, acting as a parental unit for the members of the group.

Legacy in the DC Multiverse really started to heat up in the '90s, but the JSA had already introduced their own teen legacy team in Infinity Inc. , with members like Jade, Obsidian, Hector Hall, Fury, Nuklon, Star-Spangled Kid, Brainwave II, Power Girl, and Huntress. Infinity Inc. was basically the Earth-Two Teen Titans, except they ended up working much more closely with their parents and the other older heroes way more than the Titans did with their mentors. After Crisis on Infinite Earths changed DC history, the Justice Society floundered for a while – they were trying to do the classic team in the grim and gritty early '90s and it failed – but finally found success again when it started adding legacy heroes to its ranks.

The Justice League is an army of heroes, the Teen Titans is high school, the Legion of Superheroes is a massive social club, and the Doom Patrol are the weird ones. However, the Justice Society has always been a family. When they came together, they were the only metahumans around, the only people who could understand each other. They married, had children, and brought those children up in the family business. That's as wholesome and family-friendly as you can get, but that's not all.

One thing that has changed about superheroes is their willingness to kill, especially on the big screen. Violence has always been a part of superheroes, but in the present, it's been taken to extremes. Even the Justice League has members who will kill nowadays. However, the JSA holds to its no-kill rule, even Hawkman, who always wants to kill at least one villain. The older members of the team are people of the past, brought up in a different way.

They hold their members to a higher standard, one that is more old school, and they are always there for one another – Obsidian has gone crazy numerous times and they always fight to bring him back to the light – there's a certain affection between the members of the group, one that is closer to familial love then friendship. Superhero teams are all about working together, but the Justice Society takes it to a new level. They are the first superteam and they hold each other to a higher standard, all while helping shepherd the next generation. What's more family friendly than that?

One of the most interesting parts about the Justice Society potentially being in the DCU is that you can use them to period superhero pieces. Captain America: The First Avenger took viewers to World War II and a Justice Society movie could do the same, introducing the team and pitting them against the Nazis. A superhero World War II film would do amazing numbers and that's only the beginning. You could do movies in the '50s and '60s, or take them to the present day and show them with their kids, training them to be the next generation of heroes.

If SkyDance is actually serious about wanting family friendly superheroes, and aren't just using this as a way to push their political agenda, then they need to remember the Justice Society. It's the most wholesome team in comics, full of people with old school American values helping train the next generation of heroes. They are the perfect family friend superhero team. They also have several gay members and if SkyDance wants to prove to the very left-leaning fans of superhero comics that they aren't going to destroy everything they love about DC, bringing in the JSA would go far to assuage a lot of fans' doubts. The Justice Society belong on the big screen and are the perfect new team for the SkyDance era.

Do you think that the Justice Society works as a "family friendly" team? If not, which teams would you say? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: The Sweet Way Miley Cyrus Paid Tribute To Dolly Parton During Her Beautiful Wedding Ceremony
articles.summary: Excuse me, I'm going to go grab a tissue.
articles.content:
It was reported days ago that Miley Cyrus and fiancé Maxx Morando would finally tie the knot this weekend. That was proven to be true, as Cyrus’ stepsister, Lily Purcell, recently shared some snazzy snapshots from her rehearsal dinner . Well, it’s now been confirmed that the Grammy winner and her man have officially exchanged vows. Along with that, there are also some details on the ceremony, and it was apparently quite lovely. During the event, Cyrus also paid tribute to her late godmother, Dolly Parton , in a sweet way.

For those who are unfamiliar with the song, “Love Is Like a Butterfly” is the first track on Parton’s 1974 album of the same name. It may not be the first song that people think of when they remember the late Grammy winner but, like many of her other tunes, it has worked its way into the cultural zeitgeist. Parton even performed the song with Stephen Colbert back in 2012 on an episode of The Colbert Report . All in all, it’s an incredibly sentimental song, and it’s perfect for an occasion like a wedding.

Miley Cyrus also paid tribute to her “Aunt Dolly” on multiple occasions, even doing so amid her recent performance at the Hollywood Bowl . Many have long been aware of Cyrus and Parton’s close relationship and, in 2023, the pair even collaborated musically to craft a version of Cyrus’ hit song, “Wrecking Ball”. As of late, Cyrus has also discussed the layers to Parton and even explained that people would misunderstand her authenticity as a person due to her flamboyant public persona.

Congratulations are definitely in order for Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando, and here’s wishing them a lifetime of happiness. Personally, I’d like to think that’s what Dolly Parton would want for them as well. And, while the beloved singer was not present at the ceremony, I’m glad she was able to be a small part of it in some way.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A PS5 game that normally costs $70 on the PlayStation Store is now available for $7 between now and December 1. This is the result of a gigantic 90% discount on the game. This is the biggest discount the game has ever received on the PS Store. Unfortunately, there is no PS4 version of the game, so PS4 users will not be saving an easy $63 on one of 2023's best games and one of the best horror games of the PS5 generation.

Back in 2023, at the start of the year in January, developer Motive Studio and publisher EA released a remake of one of 2008's best games and the first release in a series that had been dormant since 2013. This game and series is Dead Space . The original game is often cited as one of the best horror games of all time, and one of the great games across all genres in its generation. To this end, the original earned an 89 on Metacritic back in the day, a very good score, especially for a horror game, as horror games tend to receive slightly lower reviews than many other genres. Fittingly, the remake earned the same score and cemented itself as one of the better remakes of this current generation . Not only is it a good remake, but the original experience simply still holds up with a graphical overhaul. And it's not just critics who think this, but PS5 users on the PlayStation Store as well, hence its 4.71 out of 5 stars after more than 46,000 user reviews.

EA doesn't discount most of its games beyond 90 percent. Some end up getting the 95% discount treatment, but it's typically in annualized or semi-annualized series. To this end, we do not expect Dead Space on PS5 to be cheaper than this until its base price gets a price drop.

A Sci-Fi Survival-Horror Classic For those entirely unfamiliar with the sci-fi survival-horror game, it puts you in control of Isaac Clarke, an everyman engineer sent to repair a colossal mining ship, the USG Ishimura. Upon arrival, though, it is clear something went terribly wrong. The ship's crew is dead, and Isaac's beloved partner, Nicole, is missing somewhere on the ship. Armed with just engineering tools, Isaac has to uncover what happened and find Nicole.

Those who end up checking out Dead Space on PS5 or PS5 Pro as a result of this PlayStation Store deal should expect a runtime of about 12 to 16 hours on average, and depending largely on playstyle. Completionists, though, will need closer to 60 hours with the game.

For those who don't have $7 to spare at the moment, there is a classic PS2 series now available on the PlayStation Store for $2.24 .
